nina: Bringing up atlas-14b (int4) in staging. Quick smoke showed KV growth + p95 tailrise on long sessions.
harry: paste logs?
diego: log excerpt from staging node:
```
[2025-01-11T02:14:12Z] WARNING: KV resize requested 20MB
[2025-01-11T02:14:12Z] slab_state: free=1100 frag=51% compactions=0
[2025-01-11T02:14:12Z] request: batch=5 max_new_tokens=300 avg_seq=720
```
ciara: that frag>50% + batch=5 is a red flag for int4. We need an immediate mitigation plan before prod canary.
nina: propose rollback plan + short-term mitigations:
1) set default max_new_tokens=80 for atlas-14b-int4
2) route-level cap for /long-read -> max_new_tokens=160
3) batching.window_ms=20 and cap batch_size=3 when avg_seq>256
4) enable slot_compactor=aggressive on staging canaries
5) set prefix_cache.soft_evict_threshold=0.6
harry: also try disabling kv_prefetch for canary only; prefetch causes more concurrent KV writes and fragmentation.
diego: agreed. but slot_compactor=aggressive may bump CPU. schedule cpu watch and thermal alerts.
ciara: launching evals: eval-bucket/atlas-14b-int4-longseq vs atlas-14b-fp16. Quality gates: ROUGE-L drop <=1.2% and EM >= -0.8%.
eval-bot: Eval job queued: /evals/3135799999. Tests: long-qa, summarization-long, multi-turn retrieval QA.
nina: if eval passes, we'll keep int4 with conservative defaults and add a per-route override. if fails, rollback to fp16 and open ticket for kernel-level fragmentation mitigation.
harry: long-term: consider tuning allocator to avoid large slab slab_jitter, and add a KV growth backpressure that rejects >N concurrent KV writes per-session.
diego: I'll run a synthetic load with synthetic://long/1200 tokens and monitor slab_free and compaction runs.
ciara: adding runbook note: "atlas-14b int4 onboarding: lower max_new_tokens, batching caps, soft-evict prefix cache, slot compactor aggressive; monitor CPU".
ops-bot: Staging patch applied: atlas-14b-int4 canary -> staging-group-9 (deploy id d-5902). Monitoring enabled.
nina: thanks all — will report eval results here in ~20m. :mag:
